title: False Accusations Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Calculate how many human-written essays an AI detector wrongly flags, the share of flags that are false, and the share of false flags that fall on English-language learners.

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate how many human-written essays an AI detector wrongly flags, the share of flagged essays that are false accusations, and the share of false flags that fall on English-language learners, correctly answering three of three questions.
prerequisites: AI cheating detector, detector false positives, and bias against ELL writers, from the section "Academic Integrity and the Detector Problem" in Chapter 20.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit answers before the results unlock, then explore the inputs
keyQuestions: How many flags are true flags, and how many are wrong flags?
commonMisconceptions: A 1 percent false-positive rate means 1 percent of accusations are wrong.
A detector's errors fall evenly on all students.
A small subgroup cannot account for most of the false flags.
assessmentOpportunities: With a 1 percent false-positive rate, are 1 percent of accusations wrong?
Do a detector's errors fall evenly on all students?
What should a school do instead of relying on a detector?

controls.name: Answer box and Check
controls.description: Type a number and check it. Two tries per question.

controls.name: Next question / See the results
controls.description: Moves on after a question is finished.

controls.name: Six sliders
controls.description: Essays checked, share written by AI, sensitivity, the two false-positive rates, and the ELL share. They unlock after the questions.

controls.name: Defaults
controls.description: Puts the sliders back to their starting values.

controls.name: Start over
controls.description: Returns to Question 1 and locks the sliders.
